items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Alfred Laine Interview, 1951-04-21
items.q: I had a man by the name of Bakke, uh, Shail Bakke, uh, Bega, Lawrence Bega, uh, had, uh, uh, uh, Bill Gallaty, Willie Guitarr.

ctx.x: Jack, uh, can you remember the names of the first men that were, played music with you in your first professional band? Can you recall their names? Well, quite a number of them, I can, yes.

When I first organized, uh, uh, playing string music, and, uh, into a brass band, returned into a brass band, I had a man by the name of Bakke, uh, Shail Bakke, uh, Bega, Lawrence Bega, uh, had, uh, uh, uh, Bill Gallaty, Willie Guitarr. Now, there's a coincidence for you. This man, Willie Guitarr, that was his real name, Willie Guitarr. He played bass fiddle, and he lived on Music Street. Well, he's a mighty, mighty good bass player. Page and Mr. Ripley, huh? Exactly, exactly. Then I had... Jack, would you…
but approximately the very early bands,

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine, Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine and Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1959-02-27
items.q: His son. I never knew that, didn't he? I'm his godfather.

ctx.x: Bill Gallaty. He's playing trumpet, his son?
He played the mount harp too, don't he? His son. I never knew that, didn't he? I'm his godfather. Yeah? Yeah.
